title: Localization, stalks and the local coefficient criterion for qcqs regular functions
statement:
Let $f:Y\to T$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $\beta:\mathcal O_T\to f_*\mathcal O_Y$ be its canonical map of sheaves of rings [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. For an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq T$, put $Y_V=f^{-1}V$ and $M=\Gamma(Y_V,\mathcal O_{Y_V})$, with its structural $R$-algebra structure [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every multiplicative subset $S\subseteq R$ (containing $1$ and closed under multiplication), put $Y_{V,S}=Y_V\times_V\operatorname{Spec}(S^{-1}R)$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with $S^{-1}R$ and $S^{-1}M$ the localizations in the ordinary fraction sense [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The canonical map
$$S^{-1}M\longrightarrow\Gamma(Y_{V,S},\mathcal O),\qquad m/s\longmapsto (1/s)\,\operatorname{pr}_1^\sharp(m),$$
is an isomorphism of $S^{-1}R$-algebras, compatible with further localization and the structural coefficient maps. If $y\in V$ corresponds to $\mathfrak p\subset R$, and $A=\mathcal O_{T,y}=R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], there are canonical isomorphisms of $A$-algebras
$$(f_*\mathcal O_Y)_y\cong M_{\mathfrak p}\cong\Gamma(Y_V\times_V\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O).$$
The first sends the germ of $m/h^n$ on $D(h)$, $h\notin\mathfrak p$, to that same fraction. Their composite sends a germ to its pullback to the local base change, and identifies $\beta_y$ with the coefficient map from $A$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Moreover, $\beta$ is an isomorphism if and only if these coefficient maps are isomorphisms for all $y\in T$. When they are, every $\beta_U$ on an arbitrary open $U$ is a ring isomorphism, and its inverse commutes with restriction.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, i=0; localization and elementary fraction/germ comparison, followed by the germ-and-gluing argument for sheaf invertibility

proof.text: The restriction $f_V:Y_V\to V$ is the base change of $f$ along $V\hookrightarrow T$: by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] the inverse-image open subscheme $Y_V=f^{-1}V$, with its inclusion and the restriction of $f$, is a fibre product $Y\times_TV$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), $f_V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Since $V$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] implies that $Y_V$ is a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme. Thus it satisfies the source hypothesis of the global-sections base-change theorem, without any affineness, separatedness or Noetherian hypothesis on $Y_V$.

source.place: Tags 01K5 (lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change), 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence), 01K4 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine); affine-base reduction preceding coherent.tex Tag 02KH

proof.text: For any multiplicative subset $S\subseteq R$, the ring map $R\to S^{-1}R$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]. Consequently $g_S:\operatorname{Spec}(S^{-1}R)\to V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Both its source and target are affine. These assertions allow $0\in S$; then the source is the empty affine scheme. No finite-generation hypothesis on $S$ is used.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] to $R\to M$ and $R\to S^{-1}R$. It identifies $M\otimes_R S^{-1}R$ with the localization of $M$ at the image of $S$. This is the ordinary $S^{-1}M$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]: the fraction relations on both sides are $m/s=n/t$ iff $u(tm-sn)=0$ for some $u\in S$, with the coefficients acting through $R\to M$. Explicitly the mutually inverse maps are $m\otimes(a/s)\mapsto am/s$ and $m/s\mapsto m\otimes(1/s)$. The latter agrees with the inverse supplied by the localization isomorphism since both maps send $m/1$ to $m\otimes1$ and invert the same denominators. They preserve multiplication, since $(m/s)(n/t)=mn/(st)$. Hence this is an isomorphism of $S^{-1}R$-algebras.

source.place: Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), with the fraction construction preceding Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module)

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-global-sections-qcqs] for $X=Y_V$, $S$ there equal to $V$, and $S'$ there equal to $\operatorname{Spec}(S^{-1}R)$. Steps 1 and 2 verify all its hypotheses. Its isomorphism sends $m\otimes(a/s)$ to $\operatorname{pr}_1^\sharp(m)\operatorname{pr}_2^\sharp(a/s)$. Composing with step 3 gives the required isomorphism $\theta_S:S^{-1}M\to\Gamma(Y_{V,S},\mathcal O)$ with $\theta_S(m/s)=\operatorname{pr}_2^\sharp(1/s)\operatorname{pr}_1^\sharp(m)$. In particular $\theta_S(a/s)=\operatorname{pr}_2^\sharp(a/s)$ for $a\in R$, so it respects the specified coefficient map and is an $S^{-1}R$-algebra isomorphism, rather than merely an abstract ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02KH (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology), part (2), i=0 and F=O_X; the explicit map in the cited global-sections node

proof.text: The compatibility with further localization follows on fractions. For $S\subseteq S'$ let $q:Y_{V,S'}\to Y_{V,S}$ be the projection induced by $S^{-1}R\to(S')^{-1}R$ using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Pullback gives $q^\sharp\theta_S(m/s)=\operatorname{pr}_{2,S'}^\sharp(1/s)\operatorname{pr}_{1,S'}^\sharp(m)=\theta_{S'}(m/s)$. Every element of $S^{-1}M$ has this form. More generally, for a localization of $S^{-1}R$ at a multiplicative set of fractions, write a further denominator as $a/t$ with $t\in S$. Its inverse maps to $t/a$; both iterated maps therefore send $(m/s)/(a/t)$ to the pullback of $mt/(sa)$. Finite products of these denominators give the general case. This proves the iterated-localization compatibility by explicit multiplication, including the structural coefficients.

source.place: Tag 00CO (definition-localization), fraction arithmetic; coherent.tex Tag 02KH, explicit degree-zero map

proof.text: For $h\in R$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b) says that $D(h)$ is affine and has sections $R_h$ through restriction. Thus the affine-spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies its inclusion into $V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R_h)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$: both induce $R\to R_h$ on sections. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] to $f_V:Y_V\to V$ and the open $D(h)$, and using the uniqueness of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], identifies $Y_V\times_V\operatorname{Spec}R_h$ with $f^{-1}D(h)$. Specializing step 4 to $S=\{h^n:n\geq0\}$ now gives $\Gamma(f^{-1}D(h),\mathcal O)=M_h$, sending $m/h^n$ to the restriction of $m$ multiplied by the inverse of the restriction of $h^n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](i), the opens $D(h)$ with $h\notin\mathfrak p$ form a neighbourhood basis of $y$ inside $V$.

Put $F=f_*\mathcal O_Y$. Its sections on $U$ are $\Gamma(f^{-1}U,\mathcal O_Y)$, and $\beta$ gives compatible maps from $\mathcal O_T(U)$ by [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c) applied to the affine open $V$ of $T$, the germ map $R\to\mathcal O_{T,y}$ is a localization at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$, which identifies $A=\mathcal O_{T,y}$ with $R_{\mathfrak p}$ by $r/s\mapsto r_ys_y^{-1}$. For $s\notin\mathfrak p$, the germ $s_y=s/1$ is therefore a unit of $A$, so its image $\beta_y(s/1)$ in $F_y$ is a unit. The germ map therefore extends to a ring map $\lambda:M_{\mathfrak p}\to F_y$, $m/s\mapsto\beta_y(s/1)^{-1}m_y$. Indeed if $u(tm-sn)=0$ with $u\notin\mathfrak p$, taking germs and multiplying by the inverses of the images of $u,s,t$ gives the equality of the two proposed images. The fraction addition and multiplication formulas show this is a ring map; for $r/s\in A$ its value is $\beta_y(r/s)$, so it is $A$-linear and respects the structural algebra maps.

Every element of $F_y$ is represented by a section on a neighbourhood of $y$, by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Shrinking to $D(h)$ with $h
otin\mathfrak p$ using the basis in step 6, that section is $m/h^n$ by step 6, and its germ equals $\lambda(m/h^n)$. Thus $\lambda$ is surjective. If $\lambda(m/s)=0$, multiplication by the unit $ eta_y(s/1)$ gives $m_y=0$. The same stalk description gives a neighbourhood where $m$ restricts to zero; shrink it to $D(h)$ with $h
otin\mathfrak p$. Step 6 says $m/1=0$ in $M_h$, so the fraction relation in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $h^n m=0$ for some $n\geq0$. Since $h^n
otin\mathfrak p$, $m/s=0$ in $M_{\mathfrak p}$. Thus $\lambda$ is injective. Its inverse $F_y\cong M_{\mathfrak p}$ sends the germ represented by $m/h^n$ to that fraction, as required.

source.place: Tag 0078 (section-stalks), germ representatives and equality; algebra.tex Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module), zero criterion

proof.text: Apply step 4 to $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and use $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$ to get $\theta_{R\setminus\mathfrak p}:M_{\mathfrak p}\cong\Gamma(Y_V\times_V\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)$. Compose with the inverse of $\lambda$ from step 8. For a germ represented on $D(h)$ by $m/h^n$, the result is exactly $\operatorname{pr}_1^\sharp(m)/h^n$, the pullback of that section. Here $\operatorname{Spec}A\to V$ factors through $D(h)$ because $h$ becomes invertible in $A$: the induced ring map is $R_h\to A$, $r/h^n\mapsto r/h^n$, and the affine identifications of step 6 give that factorization. Any representative on a larger neighbourhood restricts to such a $D(h)$; equality of germs and step 8 make this independent of the restriction. For $r/h^n\in A$ (identified with $r_yh_y^{-n}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c)), the germ of $\beta_{D(h)}(r/h^n)$ goes to the coefficient $r/h^n$ in the local base change by step 4. Thus the composite identifies $\beta_y$ with precisely the asserted coefficient map.

source.place: Tag 02KH (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology), i=0; elementary comparison on fractions and germs from steps 4, 6-8

proof.text: By step 9, all local coefficient maps are isomorphisms exactly when all $\beta_y$ are isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheaf-iso-on-stalks] to the underlying sheaves of sets of $\beta$ (their stalk sets and maps are the same germs). It yields precisely that every $\beta_U$ is bijective, equivalently that the underlying sheaf map is an isomorphism. Each bijective ring map has a ring-homomorphic inverse: apply $\beta_U$ to the proposed identities for the inverse of sums, products and $1$, and use injectivity. Write this inverse as $\gamma_U$. For $W\subseteq U$ and $t\in F(U)$, naturality of $\beta$ gives $\beta_W(\gamma_U(t)|_W)=t|_W=\beta_W(\gamma_W(t|_W))$; injectivity implies $\gamma_U(t)|_W=\gamma_W(t|_W)$. Hence the inverses commute with restrictions and define the inverse as a sheaf of rings. Conversely an inverse sheaf map induces inverse stalk maps, proving both directions.
